Term1: Second recurrence of clostridioides difficile infection (cdi)
Text:
# SECOND RECURRENCE OF CLOSTRIDIOIDES DIFFICILE INFECTION (CDI)

Discontinue implicated antibiotic(s). Narrow antibiotic spectrum if antibiotic therapy is still needed. Avoid antiperistaltic agents (narcotics, loperamide, etc.). Avoid antacid therapy without clear indication. If diarrhea has improved or resolved prior to starting C. difficile treatment, consider re-assessing the diagnosis before initiating therapy. C. difficile infection usually responds to antimicrobial therapy. If symptoms do not respond to appropriate antimicrobial therapy, re-consider the diagnosis.

---

References:

Therapy:
## Inpatient

### Second Recurrence CDI:

Vancomycin Extended Pulse-Taper Regimen [M]
(Vancomycin 125 mg PO q6h for 10 days, then taper and pulse with 125 mg po q12h for 7 days, then 125mg po qday for 7 days, then 125mg every other day for 6 weeks)
< OR >
If fidaxomicin not previously used:
Fidaxomicin 200 mg po q12h for 10 days [M]
< OR>
If fidaxomicin not previously used:
Fidaxomicin Extended-Pulse Regimen [M]
(Fidaxomicin 200mg po bid x5days,then 200mg every other day x20days)

### Third or more recurrence: Consult Gastroenterology or Infectious Disease

## Outpatient

### Second Recurrence CDI:

Vancomycin Extended Pulse-Taper Regimen [M]
(Vancomycin 125 mg PO q6h for 10 days, then taper and pulse with 125 mg po q12h for 7 days, then 125mg po qday for 7 days, then 125mg every other day for 6 weeks)
< OR >
If fidaxomicin not previously used:
Fidaxomicin 200 mg po q12h for 10 days [M]
< OR>
If fidaxomicin extended-pulse regimen not previously used:
Fidaxomicin Extended-Pulse Regimen [M]
(Fidaxomicin 200mg po bid x5days,then 200mg every other day x20days)

### Third or more recurrence: Consult Gastroenterology or Infectious Disease
